current.text: He has another calf strain and is out for the preseason. It is the same injury as last season. He will probably miss the start of the regular season. Yahoo lists him as questionable (calf).
He re-signed with Charlotte for 3 years and 74 million.
Charlotte traded away LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges. White is the projected starting point guard, and the team has no backup point guard it trusts.
Experts see him as the starter over Dennis Schroder and do not think Schroder limits his minutes. Some in the market think they could share minutes, and that is one reason his ADP is low.
When healthy, he is projected for about 30 to 32 minutes or more, up from 25 last season.
Experts project 20 or more points and 5 to 7 assists as the starter.

Most experts expect his usage to dip a little from last season's very high level in Charlotte. Ball handling will be shared with Kon Knueppel and Brandon Miller, and one expert sees him as only the third or fourth usage option. Another projects about 28 usage.
Because of the new calf injury, experts now push him down to the 90s. Before the injury they took him in the 55 to 75 range.
In one auction mock he went for 13 USD, and the expert called that really good value.
A busts video lists him as a player to avoid because he is injured again. Last season he pushed to return and got hurt again.
One expert expects his FT% to bounce back this season.
Charlotte plans to space the floor and take a lot of threes.
Charlotte has only 13 back-to-backs, the league minimum. With our March 28 end date, the playoff weeks have 4, 3 and 4 games. The team has a two-game week in the matchup that starts March 1.

durable.text: He has strained his calf four times in 12 months.
His strengths are scoring, threes and free throws.
His steals and blocks are very poor. One expert says his combined steals and blocks are among the worst for any starter.
He is a streaky, inconsistent shooter. His FG% swings up and down, even though experts count him as a good shooter, including off the dribble.
He is not a pass-first point guard. He is a fine passer, but an offense cannot be built around his vision.
He attacks the paint, finishes at the rim and draws free throws.

note: When healthy, he gives a guard-friendly line of threes (2.7), FT% (85%), points and assists. The cost is FG%, turnovers and very poor steals and blocks, but no category is flagged as weak enough for a punt fit. Before the new calf strain, experts had him in the 55 to 75 range. They now push him to the 90s, which is close to his Yahoo rank of 86. The markets are cheap (Yahoo average cost 2.5 USD, ESPN 2.6 USD), while our league paid 15 USD last season and one auction mock had him at 13 USD. In a 12-team league where 144 players are drafted, he is a reasonable mid-to-late buy at a single-digit price. Early in the season, check when he returns from the calf strain, whether he gets about 30 minutes ahead of Schroder, and whether his assists reach 5 or more.
